source.filename: 2021-A Positive Pressure Jamming Based Variable Stiffness Structure and its Application on Wearable Robots.pdf

actuation: Positive pressure compressed air via miniature motor pumps
constitutive_assumptions: Jammed granules inside the annular structure are assumed to behave as a continuous beam with a circular ring cross-section under tiny deformation with no slip between granules
Granules are assumed to be evenly distributed within the chamber
Fabric material properties, surface contact friction variations, and granule-to-granule friction coefficients are treated as constant or ignored in the bending stiffness derivation
Equivalent Young's modulus is assumed to scale with the average normal force per unit cross-sectional area exerted on the granules (proportional to 1/(D^2 - d^2))
Inner rubber bladder is assumed to consume minimal elastic energy when sufficiently soft compared to the jammed granular medium
Bending angle at the joint is assumed to be negligible when calculating the torque produced by external loading on the self-locking joint
control_variables: Length of single PPJ testing specimens (50 mm)
Granular material and morphology (Shape Memory Polymer cuboids, approximately 2 mm x 2 mm x 3 mm)
Granule volume fraction (nearly 100% packing fraction to prevent bladder morphing)
Outer fabric sleeve material (single-ply non-stretchable fabric)
Displacement interval for stiffness and modulus calculation (initial 1 mm displacement during elastic deformation)
dependent_variables: Equivalent Young's modulus / bending elastic modulus (MPa)
Joint torque limit and critical slip force (N*m, N)
Sliding friction force of the sandpaper friction pad (N)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Internal pressurization of a granular chamber using an embedded pneumatic bladder enables a roughly six-fold increase in cantilever bending stiffness over an input pressure range from 68 kPa to 172 kPa.
Bending stiffness of the positive pressure jamming structure scales approximately linearly with the applied input gauge pressure.

Positive pressure jamming exhibits comparable initial elastic stiffness to vacuum-based jamming at equivalent pressure magnitudes (62 kPa), but incurs less plastic deformation and lower unloading hysteresis due to bladder elasticity.
Granular jamming provides the predominant stiffening effect, achieving 40% higher bending stiffness at 103 kPa than an air-filled cylindrical bladder of identical outer diameter.

Increasing the outer sleeve diameter increases bending stiffness via higher moment of inertia, but decreases equivalent Young's modulus due to attenuated force transmission across outer granular layers.
Increasing the inner bladder diameter increases the equivalent Young's modulus across all outer sleeve diameters due to firmer granular compaction.
Analytical modeling of jamming efficiency indicates that stiffness per unit mass is maximized when the inner bladder diameter approaches the outer fabric diameter.

Embedding sandpaper friction pads into adjacent granular chambers forms a self-locking revolute joint that permits angular adjustment between -50 degrees and +50 degrees with simultaneous shape locking and stiffening.
A lightweight wearable limb support device composed of three parallel positive pressure jamming units generates up to 15.1 N of posture-assisting force when driven by serial miniature pumps.

experimental_setup: Cantilever bending testing system using a UNITECH RB302 Microload tensile frame and DACELL load cells, with specimen clamped at one end and loaded at the tip at 20 mm/min over an 11 mm deflection range

Baseline comparative test setup measuring an unjammed rubber bladder (0 and 62 kPa), a negative pressure granular jamming unit (-62 kPa), and a positive pressure jamming module (+62 kPa) with matching dimensions (26 mm diameter, 50 mm length)
Comparison test between a sealed cylindrical pneumatic airbag and a PPJ module at 103 kPa input pressure with matched outer diameter
Pressure modulation tests evaluating a PPJ specimen under four relative pressure levels (69 kPa, 103 kPa, 138 kPa, 172 kPa) across eight repeated trials
Dimensional characterization tests across eight specimen configurations combining four outer diameters (26, 29, 32, 35 mm) and two inner diameters (10, 15 mm) under 1 atm relative pressure
Cantilever bending evaluation of a two-link PPJ system linked by a self-locking revolute joint (15 mm hinge length, friction pads) across multiple input pressures
Tensile pull-out fixture measuring sliding friction force of a sandpaper friction pad embedded in a PPJ chamber pressurized to 137 kPa

Wearable limb support test rig consisting of three parallel PPJ links (200 mm length, 20 mm diameter) pre-bent to 90 degrees and pressurized via one, two, or three miniature motor pumps in serial (100.5 kPa, 195.6 kPa, 290.1 kPa), measuring force during 10 mm displacement
future_work: Fabricating positive pressure jamming structures in non-cylindrical pre-designed geometries, such as torus shapes
Combining multiple shapes of jamming structures to form complex 3D deployable frames (e.g., tent frames)
Conducting dynamic transition tests to quantify the switching times from soft to stiff and from stiff to soft states
Investigating alternative bladder materials that reduce radial compliance and deformation under high positive pressure
Developing more durable, wear-resistant friction materials to enhance self-locking joint longevity
Incorporating internal fabric partitions inside the chamber to ensure a more uniform initial distribution of granules
independent_variables: Input relative pneumatic pressure (e.g., 62 kPa, 69 kPa, 100.5 kPa, 103 kPa, 137 kPa, 138 kPa, 172 kPa, 195.6 kPa, 290.1 kPa; -62 kPa for vacuum baseline)
Specimen configuration type (pure rubber bladder, negative pressure jamming module, pneumatic airbag, PPJ module)
Outer sleeve diameter D (26 mm, 29 mm, 32 mm, 35 mm)
Inner bladder diameter d (10 mm, 15 mm)
Bending displacement / deflection depth (up to 11 mm in cantilever tests; 10 mm in limb support tests)
Number of miniature motor pumps connected in serial (1, 2, or 3 pumps)
Pull-out displacement of the friction pad in joint friction testing
limitations_inferred: Analytical formulations for stiffness and Young's modulus assume linear beam behavior and uniform packing, which may deviate significantly under large bending deflections or cyclic loading
Operation under high positive internal pressure creates burst and leakage failure risks, particularly along adhesive seams between the silicone tube, end caps, and bladder
Dense packing (~100% volume fraction) required for effective jamming may compromise passive flexibility and softness in the unpressurized state
The friction-pad self-locking joint is constrained to single-axis planar rotation (-50 deg to +50 deg), lacking multi-axis spatial compliance without additional joint stages
Connecting multiple electric motor pumps in serial to achieve elevated pressures (up to ~290 kPa) increases power draw, weight, and acoustic noise in portable wearable scenarios
limitations_stated_by_authors: A single PPJ unit cannot achieve arbitrary shapes because its geometry is confined by the cylindrical outer fabric sleeve
Jamming performance stability and maximum reachable bending angle depend heavily on the initial distribution of granules and chamber fill percentage
The soft inner rubber bladder deforms under positive pressure, which reduces the granular jamming effect
The self-locking joint mechanism is subject to degradation over time as sandpaper friction pads lose friction through abrasive wear
Assisting force generated by the limb support prototype is slightly lower than comparable textile pneumatic literature devices lacking internal partitioning
Soft-to-stiff and stiff-to-soft state transition times were not experimentally verified
main_results: PPJ achieved approximately a six-fold increase in cantilever bending stiffness (from 0.69 N/mm to 4.02 N/mm) as input pressure rose from 68/69 kPa to 172 kPa, with exerted forces ranging from 4 N to 23 N
Stiffness exhibited a direct proportional relationship with input relative air pressure, with linear fit R^2 values of 0.992, 0.995, 0.994, and 0.993 for 69, 103, 138, and 172 kPa
At 103 kPa input pressure, the granular PPJ specimen demonstrated 40% higher bending stiffness than a pure compressed air airbag of identical outer diameter

Negative pressure jamming (-62 kPa) showed comparable initial stiffness to PPJ (+62 kPa), but saturated earlier at a maximum force and exhibited pronounced plastic deformation and hysteresis upon unloading
Enlarging outer diameter D increased bending stiffness but reduced equivalent Young's modulus due to diminished radial force transmission through outer granular layers
Enlarging inner diameter d increased equivalent Young's modulus across all outer diameters (e.g., from 1.63 MPa to 1.83 MPa at D=26 mm, and from 0.77 MPa to 0.96 MPa at D=35 mm)
Analytical modeling showed that jamming efficiency (stiffness per unit mass) is maximized when D and d converge closely

The self-locking revolute joint supported angular locking between -50 degrees and +50 degrees, displaying a two-stage load response with a joint torque limit of approximately 0.6 N*m and a friction coefficient of 1.09 under 137 kPa

The 400 g wearable limb support prototype produced initial support forces of 5.2 N, 9.4 N, and 12.8 N, and force increments at 10 mm displacement of 8.1 N, 12.4 N, and 15.1 N under one, two, and three serial pumps (100.5 kPa, 195.6 kPa, 290.1 kPa)
modeling_methods: Euler-Bernoulli cantilever beam bending stiffness formulation: K = 3EI / L^3
Ring-shaped cross-section area moment of inertia calculation: I = pi * (D^4 - d^4) / 64
Empirical/analytical equivalent Young's modulus scaling model: E = C / (D^2 - d^2) based on average cross-sectional contact force Faverage = 4Ft / [pi * (D^2 - d^2)]
Composite bending stiffness relation as a function of sleeve and bladder diameters: K = 3 * pi * C * (D^2 + d^2) / (64 * L^3)
Jamming efficiency / stiffness-to-mass optimization model: K / mass = 3 * C * (D^2 + d^2) / [16 * L^4 * rho_0 * (D^2 - d^2)]
Static torque balance formulation for the critical slip force of the self-locking joint: Fc * (L + l/2) = P * S * mu * ds and piecewise two-stage stiffness representation
performance_metrics: Equivalent Young's modulus / bending elastic modulus (MPa)
Force increment at specified deflection (N at 1 mm and 10 mm displacement)
Critical slip force Fc (N) and joint torque limit (N*m)
possible_gap_implications: Overcoming the negative 1 atm threshold via positive pressure creates opportunities for high-payload soft wearable devices, but highlights an unaddressed trade-off between pressure-bearing capacity and unpressurized compliant flexibility

The decay of equivalent modulus with increasing outer diameter reveals an inherent geometric scaling bottleneck for monolithic granular jamming columns, pointing to a need for multi-cellular or radially segmented internal architectures
The reliance on abrasive dry friction pads identifies an unresolved materials gap for self-locking soft joints requiring cyclic reliability without rapid frictional degradation

The lack of soft-to-stiff and stiff-to-soft transition dynamics underscores a research gap in characterizing control bandwidth for positive pressure granular systems relative to conventional vacuum systems
paper.research_objective: To develop and evaluate a Positive Pressure Jamming (PPJ) variable stiffness mechanism that expands the achievable stiffness range beyond the negative one atmosphere limit without altering actuator geometry, incorporate friction-pad self-locking joints for multi-configuration shape preservation, and demonstrate its feasibility in wearable limb support devices.
paper.research_problem: Negative pressure jamming approaches are physically bounded by negative one atmospheric pressure, limiting their achievable stiffness range and payload capacity, while relying on bulky vacuum pumps; furthermore, existing positive pressure approaches often couple stiffness changes with actuator bending motions or cannot conform to multiple shapes.
paper.robot_type: Wearable robot (wearable limb support device for arm and leg assistance)
stiffness_mechanism: Positive Pressure Jamming (PPJ) / granular jamming (Shape Memory Polymer granules compressed between an internal inflatable bladder and an external non-stretchable sleeve)
Friction pad self-locking revolute joint (sandpaper friction pads compressed by pressurized granules/actuator to lock joint angles)
paper.title: A Positive Pressure Jamming Based Variable Stiffness Structure and its Application on Wearable Robots
